issues.legal_issue: A pre-emptor’s failure to deposit the required price by the trial court’s deadline results in dismissal of the suit when no appellate stay relieves the pre-emptor of that obligation, and an appellate court cannot extend the deadline merely because it later changes the decree.
material_facts: The trial court decreed pre-emption for part of the land and directed the pre-emptors to deposit the required amounts by a specified deadline.
The pre-emptors did not make the deposits by that deadline.
On appeal, the lower appellate court extended the payment time while granting one pre-emptor pre-emption over an additional part of the land.
The lower appellate court had not granted a stay, and the pre-emptors had not deposited the amounts even within the extended time.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court was required to dismiss the pre-emption suit for failure to comply with the trial court’s payment directions; it could not extend the time for payment in the circumstances. The appeal was allowed and the suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Order 20 Rule 14 of the Code of Civil Procedure makes the trial court’s directions for payment mandatory. A decree under that rule imposes reciprocal obligations, so a stay relieving the defendants of their obligation to deliver possession may also relieve the pre-emptor of depositing the price while the stay operates. Merely filing an appeal does not suspend the decree, and, absent a stay, failure to deposit within the time fixed results in dismissal; an appellate court cannot extend that time merely by altering the decree. The Court relied on Naguba Appa v. Namdev, AIR 1954 SC 50, and Dattaraya s/o Keshav Tawalay v. Shaikh Mahboob Shaikh Ali, [1969] 2 SCR 514.

rule.if: preemption_proceeding and payment_required_by_trial_decree and payment_deadline_missed and no_appellate_stay

predicates.preemption_proceeding: The proceeding is a suit seeking possession by pre-emption.
predicates.payment_required_by_trial_decree: The trial court’s decree requires the pre-emptor to deposit the required price by a specified deadline.
predicates.payment_deadline_missed: The pre-emptor does not deposit the required price by the deadline fixed in the trial court’s decree.
predicates.no_appellate_stay: The appellate court has not stayed the decree in a way that relieves the pre-emptor of the deposit obligation.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption suit includes a trial decree requiring a deposit, the deadline is missed, and no appellate stay relieves the pre-emptor of payment, the suit stands dismissed.
